title: Apty Pricing: Quote-Based Digital Adoption (2026)
summary: Apty pricing relies on custom quotes, not published rates. You'll know to reach out to sales and prepare your requirements before getting an estimate.
body_markdown:
## Where Activepieces fits next to Apty


Activepieces is workflow automation, not digital adoption software, so even with 750 integrations it can't stand in for Apty and shouldn't appear in your quote comparison as an alternative to it.


That matters because a buyer squeezing a first-year budget will sometimes ask whether a cheaper tool can do the same job. It can't. The two products solve different problems, and treating them as rivals leads to a line item you can't justify later.


### How user guidance differs from system integration?


Apty sits inside your business applications and guides users through screens, fields and processes while they work.


Activepieces sits behind the scenes and moves information between systems across its 750 integrations: when something happens in one tool, it triggers an action in another, meaning most of your existing tools probably have built-in connectors.


So Activepieces doesn't replace in-app walkthroughs, on-screen prompts or task guidance; its 750 integrations connect systems, not screens, which means you still need a separate tool for in-app guidance.


If your reason for buying Apty is to change what a user does inside a screen, no workflow tool will do that for you.


Cut Apty from the budget in favour of Activepieces' $0 Free plan and you have removed the guidance and kept only the plumbing, so you're now dependent on internal expertise.


### Automation around an Apty rollout


Where the two do overlap, it is narrow but useful. Once Apty is live, you'll want adoption data and survey responses to reach the people who act on them, rather than sitting in a dashboard nobody opens.


A workflow tool can carry that data onward, and Activepieces does it at 1 credit per run however many steps the flow has, as its published pricing page states, so a flow that reads survey responses, opens a ticket and posts to team chat costs the same as one that only copies a row.


Zapier's per-task billing and Make's per-module billing both meter that three-step flow as three, while Activepieces counts it once. Its Free plan includes 1,000 credits a month and unlimited flows.


The illustration below shows the arrangement. Apty is on one side, Activepieces on the other, and one arrow carries adoption data and survey responses across, then on to a spreadsheet and a team chat tool, each reached through one of Activepieces' 750 integrations.


Take from it that the follow-up is the only part Activepieces carries, and on the $0 Free plan that is 1,000 credits a month; every piece of guidance, and the quote for it, still comes from Apty.


Before you count on this, check Apty's own pricing and documentation pages. Confirm that the export or integration route you need is included in your quote, and note the date you checked. If it's a paid extra, it belongs in your first-year total.
